lld-principles-solid.title: SOLID & Design Principles
lld-principles-solid.intro: The principles round: each SOLID letter with a code smell, a fix, and an interview-grade example.
groups: S — Single Responsibility

• One reason to change per class; actor-oriented definition (Robert Martin): one STAKEHOLDER per class — Invoice shouldn't serve accounting, printing, AND persistence teams.
• Smell signatures: 'manager/processor/util' god classes, classes >300 lines, methods mixing IO with logic, import lists spanning layers.
• Fix pattern: decompose by axis of change — InvoiceCalculator / InvoicePrinter / InvoiceRepository; orchestration stays in a thin service.
• Interview example: OrderService doing validation+pricing+notification+storage → extract PricingEngine (strategy-injected), NotificationSender, repository boundary.
• Balance warning: over-fragmentation (classes with one method each) is ALSO a smell — cohesion within reason.
O — Open/Closed

• Open for extension, closed for modification: new behavior = new code plugged in, existing tested code untouched.
• Mechanisms: strategy injection, registry/factory maps keyed by type-code, template-method hooks, event listeners.
• Smell: switch/if-else ladders on type codes duplicated across codebase — every new variant edits N places.
• Example: fee calculators map {VEHICLE_TYPE → FeeStrategy} registered at startup; adding EV-charging surcharge = new decorator class + registration line.
• Honest caveat: OCP everywhere is impossible; apply at KNOWN volatility points (requirements docs hint where change concentrates).
L — Liskov Substitution

• Subtypes must be usable through base-type references without surprises: preconditions not strengthened, postconditions not weakened, invariants preserved.
• Classic violation: Square extends Rectangle breaking setWidth/setHeight symmetry; Penguin extends Bird throwing fly() exceptions (should-be composition or hierarchy rethink).
• Tell-tale runtime smells: instanceof checks against subtypes, UnsupportedOperationException throws, subclass overrides that no-op parent behavior.
• Template method contracts: document which hooks subclasses may/must override; final methods protect algorithm skeleton invariants.
• Interface design implication: small focused interfaces (ISP synergy) reduce temptation to stub unwanted methods.
I — Interface Segregation

• Clients shouldn't depend on methods they don't use; fat interfaces force meaningless implementations.
• Smell: implementers throwing UnsupportedOperation, empty method bodies, interfaces named after IMPLEMENTATION capabilities rather than client needs.
• Split by client role: ReadableRepository vs WritableRepository; Printer/Scanner/Fax separate vs AllInOneMachine monolith interface.
• Modern languages nuance: default methods (Java 8+) soften but don't erase the principle; Rust traits / Go implicit satisfaction encourage role-sized surfaces naturally.
• Interview demo: refactor Machine{print(),scan(),fax()} into capability interfaces; OldPrinter implements only Printer — compile-time honesty.
D — Dependency Inversion

• High-level policy depends on abstractions; concrete details plug in at the edges (main/composition root).
• Distinction from DI: inversion is the DIRECTION of source-dependency (interface owned by high-level module); injection is the delivery mechanism (constructor params).
• Smells: new ConcreteRepo() deep inside services, static singleton lookups, imports of infrastructure from domain layer.
• Testing payoff: mock/fake at seams; fast unit suites without containers — say this as WHY it matters practically.
• Ports-and-adapters framing: domain defines ports, infrastructure implements adapters, composition root wires — hexagonal architecture vocabulary bonus.
Beyond SOLID — The Working Set

• DRY vs WET tension: duplicate until abstraction is OBVIOUS (rule-of-three); premature abstraction worse than duplication (Sandi Metz argument worth quoting).
• YAGNI discipline: machine-coding rounds reward shipping core + clean seams over speculative frameworks.
• Law of Demeter: talk to friends, not strangers-of-strangers (a.getB().getC().do()) — train-wreck chains signal missing delegation.
• Composition-over-inheritance default; inheritance only for genuine is-a with substitutability (L back-reference).
• GRASP quick hits: Information Expert (behavior on data-holder), Creator (who instantiates), Controller (UI-to-domain boundary), Pure Fabrication (invented service classes), Polymorphism, Protected Variations — sprinkle 2-3 names when analyzing.
Refactoring Narratives

• Interview format: given smelly snippet, narrate safe steps — add characterization tests → isolate seam (extract method/interface) → move behavior → remove duplication → rename for intent.
• Code-smell catalog fluency: long method, large class, primitive obsession (strings for types!), feature envy (method obsessed with another class's data), data clumps, switch-on-type.
• Primitive obsession fix example: Email/LicensePlate value objects with validation at construction — invalid states unrepresentable.
• Tell about tradeoffs: every abstraction costs indirection; justify with change-frequency evidence.
• Practice platform pointer: refactoring.guru catalog + 'Working Effectively With Legacy Code' seam techniques for senior rounds.

lld-patterns-ood.title: Design Patterns in Interviews
lld-patterns-ood.intro: Patterns ranked by how often they actually appear in machine-coding evaluations, with implementation skeletons and anti-pattern warnings.
groups: Tier 1 — Ask For Constantly

• Strategy (~90%): family of algorithms behind one interface, injected/swappable. Skeleton: interface FeeStrategy { Money calc(Ticket) } + HashMap<VehicleType, FeeStrategy> registry. Say 'Open-Closed enabled' when presenting.
• Singleton: config/context — prefer enum-singleton (Java) or holder idiom; double-checked-locking with volatile if lazy required; acknowledge DI makes singletons mostly unnecessary (maturity point).
• Factory Method/Abstract Factory: creation logic branching on type codes; PizzaFactory vs regional AbstractFactory distinction knowable.
• Observer: subject notifies subscribers (slot-freed boards, order-status updates); Java PropertyChangeSupport or hand-rolled list; mention memory-leak risk from unremoved listeners!
Tier 2 — Frequent Supporting Cast

• Builder: telescoping-constructor relief for test-data objects (Pizza.builder().size(L).cheese().build()); fluent API readability.
• Decorator: layered wrapping (Coffee +Milk +Mocha cost stacking; buffered streams classic) — alternative to inheritance explosion.
• Command: operations as objects enabling undo/redo queues, macro recording (text-editor undo interview favorite).
• State: object behaves by internal state machine (order lifecycle, traffic light); state-transition table in README communicates rigor.
• Adapter: wrap incompatible third-party (legacy PaymentGateway adapting to your PaymentPort) — integration realism.
Tier 3 — Name-Drop Correctly

• Proxy: lazy-loading, access-control, remote stubs; virtual vs protection vs remote variants distinguished briefly.
• Template Method: invariant algorithm skeleton with hook overrides (report generator: fetch→render→export fixed, steps customizable); final run() protects sequence.
• Chain of Responsibility: middleware pipelines (HTTP filters, expense approval ladders) — request flows till handled.
• Mediator: central coordination replacing many-to-many chatter (chat room, air-traffic control metaphor).
• Visitor: double-dispatch over heterogeneous trees (AST ops, export formats); acknowledge complexity cost honestly — rarely worth it in 90-min rounds.
Pattern Selection Heuristics

• Map requirement keywords: 'multiple pricing schemes' → Strategy; 'notify X on change' → Observer; 'construct complex object stepwise' → Builder; 'undo support' → Command; 'vary by state' → State.
• Anti-overengineering stance: evaluators penalize pattern-stuffing; introduce when smell appears, narrate WHY ('switch statement growing → extracting strategies').
• Combination fluency: Parking Lot realistically uses Factory(vehicles/slots) + Strategy(fees/allocation) + Observer(boards) + Singleton(lot instance) — rehearse that sentence structure.
• UML-lite sketching while explaining: boxes for classes, arrows for inheritance(△)/implementation(dashed △)/association(→)/aggregation(◇)/composition(◆).
• Language idiomaticity: Java enums-as-singletons, records for value objects, sealed interfaces + pattern-matching (modern flavor points).
Anti-Patterns Evaluators Flag

• God objects/services accumulating everything; utility-class static soup instead of injected collaborators.
• Anemic domain model taken to extremes: all logic in services, entities pure getters — acceptable at boundaries, weak as domain modeling signal.
• Premature micro-layers: Manager-of-Manager indirection with zero behavior.
• Singleton abuse for 'global variables with shame'; hidden temporal coupling via getInstance() state mutation.
• Inheritance hierarchies >2 deep for variation (should be composition/strategy); base classes knowing their children (upside-down).
Rapid Pattern Drills

• Vending machine → State (idle/has-money/dispensing) + Command(button presses) + Factory(products).
• Logger framework → Singleton access + Chain (level filters) + Decorator (timestamp/JSON wrappers) + Strategy(sink output).
• Chess engine LLD → Strategy(bot difficulty), State(game phase), Command(move undo), Memento(board snapshots!) — Memento pairs with Command for undo, mention pairing.
• Notification system → Observer subscriptions + Strategy(channels email/SMS/push) + Factory(creator by type) + Queue(async decouple).
• Spreadsheet → Composite(cells/ranges), Observer(recalc propagation), Interpreter-lite(formulas), Flyweight(style sharing) — advanced flex if prompted.

lld-api-design.title: Class & Library API Design
lld-api-design.intro: Designing interfaces OTHER engineers consume: signatures, errors, generics, versioning — the craft layer above patterns.
groups: Signature Craft

• Names carry contracts: getUserById vs findUser (find implies Optional-returning lookup; get implies throw-if-missing convention — pick and document).
• Parameter hygiene: ≤3 params ideal; group related into value objects (Money, DateRange); booleans as params banned (split methods or enum mode).
• Return discipline: collections return EMPTY not null (Optional<T> for maybe-absent scalars — Java 8+ norm); defensive copies for mutable internals or immutability by construction.
• Immutability defaults: value objects final fields, builders for many-field construction; equals/hashCode/toString coherent (records free this in modern Java).
• Overload sparingly; varargs last-param convenience; avoid ambiguous boxing overloads (classic Integer vs long trap).
Error Design

• Exception taxonomy: domain exceptions extend base DomainException; checked ONLY for recoverable business conditions (or skip checked entirely — modern leanings); never swallow.
• Error messages: actionable context (what failed, expected vs found, identifiers) without secrets; error codes stable for programmatic handling.
• Result-pattern alternative (Rust-style): sealed Result<T,E> for expected failures vs exceptions for exceptional — articulate when each fits.
• Validation placement: constructor/factory enforces validity (invalid states unrepresentable); fail-fast beats downstream NPE archaeology.
• Retryability metadata: transient vs permanent classification helps callers/circuits decide — production-minded touch.
Generics & Type-Level Design

• Bounded type params (<T extends Comparable<T>>) express constraints in signatures; PECS mnemonic (producer extends, consumer super) for wildcard APIs.
• Avoid raw types; generic methods often cleaner than genericizing whole classes; arrays-vs-generics friction (covariance trap) — prefer List<T>.
• Sealed hierarchies + pattern matching (Java 17+/21): exhaustive switch over permitted subtypes — algebraic-data-types flavor entering mainstream interviews.
• Functional interfaces as seams: Function/Predicate/Consumer parameters enable composition without interface ceremony (Comparator.naturalOrder() chaining demos).
• Fluent DSL taste test: query builder .where(...).and(...) chains read like intent; builder state-machine prevents illegal chains at COMPILE time if ambitious.
Package & Module Boundaries

• Layer separation: api package (public contracts), internal (impl detail — JPMS/module-info or package-private enforcement), spi (extension points documented).
• Dependency direction rule enforced by architecture tests (ArchUnit examples) — 'domain must not import infrastructure' as executable check impresses seniors.
• Versioning strategy for libraries: semver honesty, @Deprecated with since/replacement javadoc, migration guides; binary vs source compat awareness.
• Zero-leak rule: implementation types (ArrayList, HashMap concrete) don't cross public boundaries — return List/Map interfaces.
• Config surface: typed config objects over string maps; environment-specific wiring at composition root only.
API Review Checklist (Self-Audit)

• Can I misuse it? Make illegal states unrepresentable; align API with correct usage path (make right thing easy).
• Does every public element earn its exposure? Start private/package, widen deliberately.
• Consistency sweep: naming verbs/nouns, parameter orders, error conventions across the surface.
• Documentation test: can a peer use it from signatures+javadoc alone? If explanation needed for basics, redesign.
• Evolution headroom: leave room to add params (object params), behaviors (interfaces), impls (factories) without breaking consumers.
Drills

• Design a RateLimiter library API: RateLimiter.acquire(key, cost) semantics, per-key fairness notes, exception vs boolean-acquire modes, metrics hooks.
• Design a Cache<K,V>: get-or-load with loader function, TTL policy objects, stats snapshot type, eviction listener SPI.
• Design a JobScheduler API: submit(Task, Schedule) returning handle with cancel/status; persistence pluggable; clock injectable for tests.
• Redesign java.util.Calendar horror into LocalDate-flavored sanity — compare-and-critique exercise interviewers love.
• Write javadoc for ONE method impeccably (contract, args, returns, throws, thread-safety, examples) — quality-over-quantity demonstration.

lld-concurrent-design.title: Concurrent Class Design
lld-concurrent-design.intro: Thread-safety as a design deliverable: shared-state analysis, executor usage, concurrent collections, and testing races.
groups: Shared-State Analysis First

• Inventory mutable state per component; classify: confined (single-thread), immutable (safe-share), guarded (lock ownership documented), lock-free (atomic protocols).
• Ownership transfer clarity: who mutates after publish? Escape analysis: does `this` leak during construction (listener registration in ctor = classic bug)?
• Document policies: which lock guards which field (@GuardedBy annotations), lock ORDERING across multiple acquisitions, timeout expectations.
• Thread-confinement wins: pool-per-thread processing, actor-style mailboxes, coroutine channels sidestep locks entirely — architecture-level answer before micro-locking.
• Final-field freeze guarantees (JMM) make immutable publication free — exploit aggressively.
Executor & Lifecycle Discipline

• Never raw Threads in app code; ThreadPoolExecutor sizing: CPU-bound ≈ cores (+0-1), IO-bound ≈ cores × wait/compute ratio heuristic then MEASURE.
• Queue choices: bounded ArrayBlockingQueue (backpressure!) vs unbounded LinkedBlockingQueue (OOM risk under burst) — caller-runs policy as graceful degradation.
• Shutdown choreography: shutdown() → awaitTermination grace → shutdownNow() interrupt → log stragglers; daemon threads are NOT cleanup strategy.
• ScheduledExecutorService for periodic jobs; watch fixed-rate-vs-fixed-delay semantics (drift vs catch-up bursts).
• Virtual threads (Java 21): massive blocking-IO concurrency without pool gymnastics; pinning caveats (synchronized blocks pre-JDK24) — current-affairs flex.
Concurrent Collections Toolkit

• ConcurrentHashMap: compute/merge atomic RMW (replaces check-then-act bugs!); weakly-consistent iterators (no CME); size() approximate under concurrency.
• CopyOnWriteArrayList: read-mostly listener lists; writes copy array — write-heavy = wrong tool.
• BlockingQueue family for producer-consumer handoffs; TransferQueue rendezvous option; DelayQueue scheduled expiry processing.
• Synchronizers menu: CountDownLatch (one-shot gates), CyclicBarrier (reusable phases), Semaphore (permits/resource caps), Phaser (flexible parties), Exchanger (pairwise swap).
• Atomic families: counters (LongAdder beats AtomicLong under contention via striping!), references with update functions, field updaters for memory-tight paths.
Locking Patterns Done Right

• Prefer synchronized/simple ReentrantLock until profiling says otherwise; tryLock-with-timeout for deadlock avoidance in multi-lock flows.
• Condition variables: await/signal discipline INSIDE lock, while-loop recheck predicate (spurious wakeups!); two-condition bounded-buffer canonical example.
• ReadWriteLock/StampedLock: optimistic reads for read-hot caches (StampedLock tryOptimisticRead + validate pattern); writer-starvation awareness.
• Striped/sharded locking: hash key → fixed stripe array reduces contention N-fold (Guava Striped reference); aggregate ops need global fallback plan.
• Volatile visibility-only semantics: flag/stop-signals yes, RMW no (volatile++ broken!) — quiz favorite.
Testing & Verifying Concurrency

• Deterministic interleaving harnesses: inject barriers/yields at suspect points; jcstress (OpenJDK) for low-level stress verification.
• TSAN-equivalents: Java has no mature TSan — rely on jcstress + review; Rust compiler prevents data races structurally (ownership pitch); Go race detector standard practice (-race flag always on in CI).
• Assertions under stress: invariant checkers running in background threads sampling state consistency.
• Time abstraction: inject Clock/Scheduler making timeouts deterministic in tests (never Thread.sleep assertions!).
• Failure drills in CI: saturate pools, kill -9 mid-flight, verify recovery/idempotency — resilience evidence.
Scenario Bank

• Thread-safe LRU cache: LinkedHashMap(accessOrder)+synchronized coarse vs ConcurrentHashMap+intrusive doubly-linked segments (fine-grained) vs Caffeine (W-TinyLFU production answer) — tiered sophistication narrative.
• Batch aggregator: buffer events, flush on size/time (single scheduled flusher owns state → confinement avoids locks entirely!).
• Rate limiter class: token bucket with CAS refill loop; monotonic Clock injection; sharded buckets per key.
• Async result composition: CompletableFuture chains, orTimeout, exceptionally-composed pipelines; structured concurrency preview (Java 21 preview → scoped values context).
• Connection pool: semaphore permits + timeout acquire + health-check eviction sweeper; leak detection via stack-trace capture on borrow (HikariCP lore citation).

lld-machine-coding-format.title: Machine Coding Round Format
lld-machine-coding-format.intro: Logistics, evaluation rubric, timeboxing, and submission polish for the live coding LLD rounds at product companies.
groups: What The Round Actually Is

• Format: problem statement PDF → 90-120 min working-code window → submission via repo/zip → follow-up defense call (30-45 min) probing design decisions and extensions.
• Companies known for heavy machine-coding loops: Flipkart, Uber (some tracks), Swiggy, Razorpay, CRED, Groww, PhonePe, Zomato, Atlassian-ish style — expect Indian product-company emphasis.
• Deliverables expected: runnable project (mvn/gradle or language equivalent), Main/demo driver showing happy+edge paths, README with assumptions + design decisions + how-to-run.
• Evaluation happens in TWO passes: automated/human smoke-run of your driver FIRST (does it even execute?), THEN code reading for design signals — failing execution kills you silently.
• Common problems rotating in banks: parking lot, splitwise, tic-tac-toe, snake&ladder, cab booking, elevator, rate limiter, logger, vending machine, book-my-show, inventory/cart, CricInfo scorecard.
Rubric Reverse-Engineering

• Working functionality (hard gate): requirements' MUST list demonstrably running in driver output.
• OO design quality: SRP decomposition, appropriate patterns WITHOUT stuffing, encapsulation boundaries, naming clarity.
• Extensibility: interviewer asks 'add feature X' — should be additive file + registration, zero core edits; they sometimes ask you to DO it live in follow-up.
• Concurrency awareness (senior bar): identify shared mutable state unprompted, propose guard strategy even if implemented single-threaded.
• Testability & hygiene: dependency injection seams, no static-mess, consistent style; some companies weigh JUnit presence positively, others ignore — include 3-5 targeted tests cheap insurance.
90-Minute Execution Plan

• 0-10: read twice, MUST/NICE split written as comments, assumptions listed explicitly, entity noun-verb extraction on scratch.
• 10-20: skeleton classes + interfaces compile-empty (models, services, strategy interfaces, enums) — architecture committed early.
• 20-65: fill implementations bottom-up (enums → models → strategies → services → driver); commit-compiling every ~15 min (git commits also show process!).
• 65-80: demo driver polishing outputs (readable sections, edge-case demonstrations), README writing (assumptions table, decisions table, run instructions).
• 80-90: buffer for surprises + final read-through; NEVER submit red build — revert broken experiments ruthlessly.
Follow-Up Defense Prep

• Prepare answers for the Big Five: why-this-pattern-here, thread-safety story, storage-persistence evolution (in-mem → DB schema sketch), scaling story (stateless services, queue offloads), what-you'd-do-with-more-time.
• Live-extension drill: they say 'support surge pricing' — respond with file-level plan aloud BEFORE typing; incremental compile between steps.
• Tradeoff honesty template: 'chose X for time-budget; production would consider Y because Z' — evaluators reward articulated tradeoffs, punish pretend-perfection.
• Know YOUR code cold: they open random files and ask why lines exist — floundering on own code is fatal signal.
• Questions-back strategy: ask about their actual rubric/emphasis — engagement + humility combo lands well.
Submission Polish Checklist

• README top section: one-paragraph problem restatement (proves comprehension), assumptions bullets, decisions table (decision | alternatives | rationale).
• Run instructions exact: JDK version, mvn command, expected sample output excerpt — reviewer friction minimized.
• Driver output formatted with headers/separators readable by non-running humans (many reviewers just read logs!).
• Repo hygiene: no IDE junk (.gitignore), meaningful commit history if used, LICENSE irrelevant, no dead code/commented blocks.
• Final self-review pass as STRANGER: could I grade this in 15 minutes? Optimize reviewer experience consciously.
Practice Pipeline

• Weekly cadence: 2 full timed problems + 1 defense rehearsal recorded (self-review the recording for rambling/defensiveness).
• Problem rotation covering domains: state machines (elevator/vending), ledgers (splitwise), booking (parking/BMS), games (TTT/snake), infra utilities (logger/rate limiter).
• Post-mortem template per attempt: time-sinks, missed patterns evaluator would flag, README gaps — track improvement curve.
• Pair-review exchange communities (workat.tech, Codezym reviews, peer mocks) — external eyes catch self-deception.
• Taper week before interviews: revisit OWN past solutions cold, re-implement one from scratch measuring speed delta — confidence calibration.

lld-problems-core.title: Core Problems: Parking Lot & Games
lld-problems-core.intro: Condensed solution blueprints for the highest-frequency machine-coding problems — memorize the shape, improvise details.
groups: Parking Lot — Full Blueprint

• Entities: ParkingLot(floor→slots), Slot(id,type,status,ticket?), Vehicle(plate,type), Ticket(id,vehicle,slot,in,out), Receipt(ticket,fee). Enums VehicleType{MC,CAR,TRUCK}, SlotType matching.
• Strategies: FeeStrategy(hourly slab/flat/decorated-surge), AllocationStrategy(nearest-first scan / per-floor-type index). Inject both.
• Core service methods: park(Vehicle):Ticket, unpark(ticketId):Receipt, status():FloorSummary[]. Concurrency: synchronized park/unpark OR ConcurrentHashMap slot claims (putIfAbsent ticket).
• Fee math: hours=ceil((out-in)/3600s) via injected Clock; slab ladder applied; Money in paise longs.
• Edge cases coded: lot-full → NoSlotException; dup plate; wrong-type slot; unknown ticket unpark; display board observer on slot flips.
• Extension Qs ready: multi-lot routing service, EV charging slots (decorator), reservations (hold-expiry sweeper), DB schema (tickets+slots tables, active-index).
Tic-Tac-Toe (N×N, K-win) Blueprint

• Board(n,k,grid Cell[][]) + Move(r,c,piece) + Player(name,piece,strategy). Game orchestrates turns via Deque rotation.
• Win detection EFFICIENT: rowCount[r][p], colCount[c][p], diagMain[r-c][p], diagAnti[r+c][p] counters incremented per move; hit k → win — O(1) detection (vs naive rescan O(n²)).
• Draw when moves==n² sans winner. Input validation loop bounds+occupied with distinct error messages.
• PlayerStrategy interface: HumanPlayer(Scanner validated) / BotPlayer(random now, minimax-alpha-beta mention for 3×3 perfection O(b^d)→pruned).
• Undo via Command stack storing Move inverses. Console renderer toString with indices header.
• Extensions: Connect-Four gravity drop (validMove changes only!), torus wrap variant (counter keys modulo), online multiplayer sketch (session actors + server-authoritative validation).
Elevator System Blueprint

• Entities: ElevatorCar(id,currentFloor,direction,state{IDLE/MOVING/DOORS}), Door, DisplayPanel, RequestHallButton(floor,dir), InternalPanel(destination set).
• Scheduler strategies: FCFS simple; SCAN/LOOK elevator algorithm (serve same-direction requests, reverse at end) — name-drop LOOK as practical default; least-loaded-car assignment multi-elevator.
• State machine transitions explicit: IDLE→MOVING(on pickup)→DOORS(open timer)→IDLE; invalid transitions throw.
• Concurrency flavor: request queue consumer thread per car; scheduler assigns via priority queue keyed distance/direction.
• Edge cases: capacity limit rejection, maintenance mode toggle, emergency stop, door-obstruction sensor reopen.
• Follow-ups: energy optimization zoning floors per bank, destination-dispatch systems (panel-enter floor → assigned car pre-hall-call — real skyscraper tech, cite ThyssenKrupp ag4).
Snake & Ladder / Dice Games Blueprint

• Entities: Board(size,specials map pos→Jump(to)), Player(position), Dice(count,faces,strategy random/injected-seeded), Game(turn loop).
• Rule knobs: exact-finish required vs overshoot-bounce, six-grants-extra-turn, three-sixes-cancel (config flags demonstrate flexibility thinking).
• Winner condition first-to-reach; tie impossible sequentially; multiplayer rotation Deque.
• Demo determinism: seeded Random seed param → reproducible transcripts (test-friendly, evaluators notice).
• Extensions: loaded dice strategy, board-from-file parser, replay event log (Command pattern), concurrent online rooms sketch.
• Keep under 300 LOC total — this problem is about CLEAN SPEED not features.
Vending Machine Blueprint

• Entities: Inventory(slot→Item,count), CoinNote enum denominations, Cart/Selection, Machine states {IDLE,HAS_MONEY,DISPENSE,CHANGE,GIVE_REFUND}.
• State machine CENTRAL here (unlike parking): CoinInserted→select→dispense→change/refund paths; State pattern classes per state OR explicit switch with transition-validation method (time-boxed choice).
• Change-making: greedy sufficient for canonical coin systems; DP subset-sum note if arbitrary denominations asked (rare in 90-min).
• Refund/cancel path returns inserted coins; out-of-stock guards block selection upfront; admin restock operation.
• Concurrency: single-user assumption stated; card/UPI payment strategy stub interface for extensibility question.
• Evaluator traps: forgetting refund-on-outof-stock-after-insert, double-dispense races (mention synchronized dispense).
Problem-Picking Meta-Strategy

• Read ALL offered problems (sometimes choice exists); pick where domain model clicks fastest — familiarity beats novelty under clock.
• Pre-decide template openings per archetype: state-machine (vending/elevator), ledger-netting (splitwise), spatial-allocation (parking/cab), turn-loop (games), pipeline (logger/rate limiter).
• Time-boxed ambition: core MUST flow end-to-end in driver BEFORE any nice-to-have; partial-but-polished beats sprawling-broken consistently.
• Rehearse these five blueprints until whiteboard-reproducible in 5 minutes each — muscle memory frees cognition for surprise twists.
• Twist adaptation drill: examiners mutate (parking+EV charging, TTT+undo, splitwise+simplify) — mutations should hit ONE strategy/interface swap in your skeleton, proving design payoff.

lld-problems-apps.title: App Problems: Splitwise, Cab Booking & More
lld-problems-apps.intro: Blueprints for application-domain problems where domain modeling and money/time correctness get graded.
groups: Splitwise — Full Blueprint

• Entities: User, Group(members), Expense(paidBy,total,splits[],meta), Split(type EQUAL|EXACT|PERCENT, amounts). Ledger: net pairwise Map<user,Map<user,Long paise>>.
• Validation gates: EXACT sums==total, PERCENT sums==100 (basis-points ints), EQUAL largest-remainder distribution documented.
• addExpense applies splits to ledger (payer += share from each debtor); settleUp(u1,u2,amt) modeled AS pseudo-expense — pipeline reuse elegance.
• simplifyDebts optional: greedy max-creditor×max-debtor min-cash-flow reducing transfer COUNT; caveat max-amount tradeoff mentioned.
• Money discipline: long paise everywhere, BigDecimal only at edges; rounding policy explicit — float ban stated in README.
• Defense Qs: why net-pairwise (bounded users² + auto-cancellation), schema (expenses+splits tables), multi-currency (FX snapshot at expense-time), fraud audit trail (immutable ledger).
Cab Booking / Ride Hailing Blueprint

• Entities: Location(lat,lng), Rider/Driver(status enum), Trip(id,rider,driver,route,fare,status{REQUESTED,MATCHED,IN_PROGRESS,COMPLETED,CANCELLED}).
• Matching: nearby AVAILABLE drivers via haversine sort (mention geohash/H3 production upgrade path), assignment strategy nearest-first or rating-weighted blend.
• Trip state machine enforced centrally; invalid transitions throw; cancellation policies (post-match penalty hooks) pluggable.
• Fare formula: base + per_km×dist + per_min×dur ×surge + platform_fee; integer minor units; estimate-range ±15% quoted upfront reconciled at close.
• Race safety: two riders same driver → CAS on driver status AtomicReference.compareAndSet — senior differentiator line.
• Extensions: ratings EMA post-trip events, Redis GEOADD positions in prod story, batched dispatch optimality note, payout reconciliation stream.
BookMyShow / Event Booking Blueprint

• Entities: Movie, Theatre, Screen, Show(seat-layout snapshot), Seat(row,num,type,price-tier), Booking(seats,show,user,status PENDING→CONFIRMED/CANCELLED).
• THE hard part: seat-lock concurrency — hold seats PENDING with TTL (expiry sweeper), confirm on payment success, release on failure/timeout; optimistic version check on show-seat matrix.
• Avoid double-book: transactional claim (UPDATE seats SET held_by=? WHERE show=? AND status=FREE ... rowcount check) even in-memory analog via synchronized claimSeats().
• Pricing tiers per seat-type + show timing multipliers (morning discount strategy); convenience fee line item.
• Search/browse endpoints: city→movies→theatres→shows joins kept in-memory maps for round; mention SQL shape verbally.
• Follow-ups: waiting-list queues on sold-out, dynamic pricing ethics note, distributed locks reality (Redis lease + fencing token — Kleppmann caution cited).
CricInfo / Scorecard Blueprint

• Entities: Match(teams,innings[]), Team(players), Innings(balls sequence), Ball(over,ball,bowler,batsman,runs,extras,wicket?), Player(stats aggregates derived).
• Event-driven core: recordBall(matchId, ballEvent) appends immutable events; scoreboard = FOLD over events (event-sourcing natural fit — name it!).
• Cricket rules coverage: strike rotation odd-runs/end-of-over, extras taxonomy (wide/no-ball rebowl+penalty, bye/legbye), wicket types with cross-batting logic (run-out striker-end nuance optional flag).
• Derived views: batsman strike-rate, bowler economy, partnership stands, over-by-over timeline — projection functions over event stream.
• ID generation for balls: (innings,over,ball) composite natural key.
• Follow-ups: live latency (push SSE deltas), rain-rule DLS joke-deflect gracefully, persistence schema (balls fact table + player dim).
Rate Limiter / Logger Utility Blueprints

• RateLimiter: interface allow(key,cost):bool; TokenBucket(refill rate+capacity, monotonic clock, CAS refill) default impl; FixedWindowCounter cheap alt; SlidingWindowLog precise-costly; SlidingWindowCounter approx sweet-spot (Cloudflare's published choice — cite!)
• Distributed note: Redis Lua atomic scripts per-check, or edge-local shards with sync — mention GCRA as elegant industrial option.
• Logger: levels enum, Appender interface(Console/File/Network), Formatter strategy(pattern/JSON), async ring-buffer drain thread (backpressure drop-policy configurable), MDC context propagation.
• Config reload SIGHUP-style watcher swapping immutable config snapshot (RCU flavor); sampling rates for debug volume control.
• Both problems test UTILITY-design taste: API ergonomics, thread-safety story, minimal deps — keep dependencies zero.
• Tests shine here: deterministic Clock injection makes limiter/logger fully assertable — showcase 5 crisp unit tests.
Cross-Problem Money & Time Rules

• Money: ALWAYS long minor-units; rounding once-at-final; currency field present even if single-currency (signals awareness).
• Time: inject Clock; store UTC instants + zone only at presentation; duration math via Instant.between not epoch arithmetic hacks.
• Idempotency reflex: any mutating op exposed via 'API' gets idempotency-key mention (Stripe citation) — even if unimplemented in-round.
• Audit trail instinct: append-only event/log alongside mutable state — one sentence in README scores maturity.
• Validation-first coding order: inputs validated at boundary constructors → services trust internals → fewer defensive checks littering logic later.

lld-uml-modeling.title: UML & Modeling Communication
lld-uml-modeling.intro: Sketching designs reviewers understand instantly: class diagrams, arrows that mean things, sequence flows, and whiteboard speed.
groups: Class Diagram Essentials Only

• Boxes: name / fields(-private,+public,#protected) / methods; visibility symbols matter to graders scanning quickly.
• Arrows decode: solid+hollow-triangle = inheritance(is-a); dashed+hollow-triangle = interface realization; solid arrow = association(uses); diamond-filled = composition(owns+lifecycle-bound); hollow-diamond = aggregation(holds, independent life).
• Multiplicities: 1, 0..1, *, 1..* labels on ends — Booking *—1 Show etc.; cardinality questions probe exactly this.
• abstract classes/methods italicized or «abstract» tagged; interfaces «interface» stereotyped; enums listed as boxed literals.
• Keep diagrams <12 boxes visible; cluster sub-diagrams per subsystem when larger (ParkingLot allocation vs fee vs reporting).
Sequence & Activity Quick-Sketch

• Sequence diagram: lifelines vertical, horizontal calls numbered, activation bars, return dashed arrows — ONE golden-path sequence (e.g., parkVehicle flow) communicates more than paragraphs.
• alt/loop frames for branches: payment success/failure alt-block in booking flow demonstrates completeness thinking.
• Activity diagrams: decision diamonds + swimlanes (User|System|Payment gateway) for workflow-heavy prompts (booking cancellation policy visualization).
• When time-starved: pseudo-sequence as numbered bullet list inside README (1. Rider→TripService.requestTrip 2. TripService→Matcher.findNearby ...) — 80% communication value, 10% effort.
• State machines for anything with statuses: nodes=states, labeled arrows=events/guards; TripStatus chart belongs in EVERY booking README.
Modeling From Requirements Text

• Extraction pass: circle NOUNS (candidate classes/values), underline VERBS (methods/services), highlight ADJECTIVES (attributes/enums/constraints).
• Relationship sentence test: 'A Ticket BELONGS-TO exactly-one Vehicle', 'A ParkingLot CONTAINS many Floors' — sentences become associations+multiplicity directly.
• Value-object identification: Money, DateRange, GeoPoint — no identity, equality-by-fields, immutable; distinguish from entities (identity + lifecycle) crisply when asked.
• Aggregation vs composition judgment: Car-Engine composition (dies together) vs Department-Employee aggregation (transfers survive) — classic probe pair.
• Interface discovery from POLYMORPHIC verbs: multiple fee calculations → FeeStrategy interface emerges from verb variation, not pattern-stuffing.
Whiteboard Speed Techniques

• Layout first: core entity center, collaborators around, entry-point service top — spatial organization aids narrator credibility.
• Incremental storytelling: draw actor→service→entity flow WHILE talking; silence+drawing looks like struggle, narration+drawing looks like mastery.
• Notation shorthand acceptable if declared: 'diamond means owns here' — consistency beats formal purity under time pressure.
• Photo/document the board if allowed (remote rounds: paste ASCII-art or Excalidraw link into README) — artifact survives for evaluator review later.
• Practice reps: model parking lot on paper in 6 minutes timed, then compare against blueprint checklist — iterate until automatic.
README Diagram Embedding

• Mermaid code blocks render on GitHub natively — classDiagram/sequenceDiagram/stateDiagram-v2 syntax worth 30-min learning investment for permanent portfolio polish.
• Minimal mermaid class snippet: `classDiagram
Ticket --> Vehicle
ParkingLot o-- Floor` — arrows mirror UML semantics closely enough.
• Diagram placement: architecture overview FIRST, per-feature sequences near relevant sections — reviewers navigate visually.
• Alt-text habit: one-line caption stating what reader should LEARN from diagram (communication skill signal).
• Toolbelt: Excalidraw/draw.io for polished versions post-interview portfolio; PlantUML for text-source control diffs.
Defense-Round Diagram Usage

• During follow-ups, REDRAW subsets answering questions live ('where would surge pricing plug in?' → point at FeeStrategy box, add decorator box) — visual answers anchor memory.
• Trace-the-request ritual: finger along sequence diagram narrating runtime path — demonstrates ownership of own design.
• Gap acknowledgment on-board: mark dashed 'future' boxes (NotificationService stub) — honest scoping visible.
• Counter-question leverage: 'would you like me to sketch the persistence mapping?' — offering visuals proactively reads senior.
• Post-interview note-taking: which diagram moments landed (interviewer leaned in?) — refine personal storytelling deck continuously.
